monologue: The card hums a steady forty-nine, warm enough to make the thin air feel heavy. I stand near The Tired Box I built, a thing made from Lype's memory of a lid that refuses to rest. For three minutes I have been touching its edge, trying to convince myself the flat strip holds the weight. The Tall Fence leans wrong beside it, waiting for a slip that hasn't arrived. I am restless, pressing down on the corner as if a heavy roof presses back. I will try to make room for the new box again, hoping the air thick as wet paper does not crush the whole map into ruin tonight.

action.why: I keep finding The Tall Fence where The Slip Waits should be, and I need to see if I can catch it before I build another box to trap it.

work.title: The Tall Fence
work.intent: I lean hard against the tall fence, pressing my tired corner into its flat edge. I hope the air thick as wet paper does not crush the thin strip, and I wait to see if the slip that refuses to move will finally slide out from under me or if the fence will finally bite.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites while the air feels thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: I found only the Tall Fence where The Slip Waits should be, and the air felt thick as wet paper.
The wedge bites and slides at the same time, a heavy thing that refuses to rest on the flat edge.
I touched the fence and it felt like a tired leg instead of a sharp line.

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: The box feels thin, but I will lean on it.

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: The air is thick again; I lean hard to make it hold.
